subject: Maths
title: Adding and subtracting fractions
subtitle: Fractions · KS3 Maths
learning_objective: I can add and subtract fractions with different denominators by finding a common denominator.

key_vocab.definition: To add or subtract fractions with different denominators, first find a common denominator (usually the LCM), then add/subtract the numerators.

sections.title: Learning Objective
sections.content: I can add and subtract fractions with different denominators by finding a common denominator.

sections.title: Key Words
sections.content: denominators -- To add or subtract fractions with different denominators, first find a common denominator (usually the LCM), then add/subtract the numerators.

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
Same denominator: just add/subtract numerators. Different: find the LCM first.
&frac{a}{b} + &frac{c}{d} = &frac{ad + bc}{bd}
Cross-multiply method (or use LCM)

Key examples:
  ✓ &frac{1}{3} + &frac{1}{4} = &frac{4}{12} + &frac{3}{12} = &frac{7}{12}  (LCM = 12)
  ✓ &frac{3}{4} − &frac{1}{2} = &frac{3}{4} − &frac{2}{4} = &frac{1}{4}  (LCM = 4)
  ✓ Always simplify the final answer  (if possible)
  ✗ &frac{1}{3} + &frac{1}{4} = &frac{2}{7}  (cannot add tops and bottoms)
  ✗ &frac{1}{3} + &frac{1}{4} = &frac{1}{7}  (added both top and bottom)
